items.hook: First radio-frequency identification (RFID) human implantation tested in the United Kingdom.
items.body: Radio-frequency identification (RFID) uses electromagnetic fields to automatically identify and track tags attached to objects. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: In San Fernando, Tamaulipas, Mexico, 72 illegal immigrants are killed by Los Zetas and eventually found dead by Mexican authorities.
items.body: San Fernando is a city located in the Mexican state of Tamaulipas; it serves as the seat of the surrounding municipality of the same name. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: The Ocean, previously known as the Ocean Limited, is a passenger train operated by Via Rail in Canada on its Atlantic Canada route between Montreal, Quebec, and Halifax, Nova Scotia.
items.body: It is the oldest continuously operated named passenger train in North America. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.hook: It is served by the S-Bahn lines S3, S41, S42, S46, S5, S7 and S9 and so represents a major interchange point on the Berlin S-Bahn network.
items.body: Berlin Westkreuz is a station in the Charlottenburg district of Berlin. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: The Guild of the Brave Poor Things was a British charity for disabled children.
items.body: It was established in 1894 by Dame Grace Kimmins (1871–1954) et al. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: The Australian Antarctic Territory is created.
items.body: The Australian Antarctic Territory (AAT) is a region of East Antarctica claimed by Australia as an external territory. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.hook: The Panic of 1857 begins, setting off one of the most severe economic crises in United States history.
items.body: The Panic of 1857 was a financial crisis in the United States caused by the declining international economy and over-expansion of the domestic economy. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: Agni Air Flight 101 crashes near Shikharpur, Makwanpur, Nepal, killing all 14 people on board.
items.body: Agni Air Flight 101 was a regional flight between Kathmandu and Lukla, Nepal, that crashed on 24 August 2010, killing all 14 people on board. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.body: Teona Strugar Mitevska, Céline Sciamma, Blerta Basholli and Jelena Maksimović were in discussion at Sarajevo.

items.hook: The Giant Powder Company was an explosives manufacturing company which operated from the mid 19th century through the first half of the 20th century, located in the San Francisco Bay Area of California.
items.body: The Giant Powder Company was the first company in the United States to produce dynamite under an exclusive license from Alfred Nobel. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: Greenland meltwater is intensifying European heatwaves
items.body: The cooling of the North Atlantic is creating waviness in the jet stream and high-pressure ridging over Europe, a study finds

items.hook: The 1662 Book of Common Prayer is legally enforced as the liturgy of the Church of England, precipitating the Great Ejection of Dissenter ministers from their benefices.
items.body: The 1662 Book of Common Prayer is an authorised liturgical book of the Church of England and other Anglican bodies around the world. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.hook: Polidoro Caldara, usually known as Polidoro da Caravaggio, was an Italian painter of the Mannerist period, "arguably the most gifted and certainly the least conventional of Raphael's pupils", who was best known for his now-vanished paintings on the facades of Roman houses.
items.body: He was unrelated to the later painter Michelangelo Merisi da Caravaggio, usually known just as Caravaggio, but both came from the town of Caravaggio. One of those things you can't un-know.
